segregation.statement: No affected relative carrying the variant is reported. 40574834 reports low-level somatic mosaicism (10.06% in peripheral blood) in the mother of patient 3; the mosaic individuals were asymptomatic and not considered to have HA20. The text does not name the mother's variant explicitly.

quotes.quote: Additionally, genetic analysis of family members revealed two cases of low frequency somatic mosaicism of TNFAIP3 in peripheral blood, with 10.06% in the mother of patient 3 and 16.7% in the father of patient 18 (3).
The two patients with somatic mosaicism of TNFAIP3 variants were asymptomatic.

de_novo.statement: Not reported as tested for de novo status. The mother carries low-level somatic mosaicism (10.06%) per 40574834; father's testing is not reported.

quotes.quote: Additionally, genetic analysis of family members revealed two cases of low frequency somatic mosaicism of TNFAIP3 in peripheral blood, with 10.06% in the mother of patient 3 and 16.7% in the father of patient 18 (3).

functional.statement: 40574834 states that patient 3 shows exon 8 skipping (p.H636fsX), but its minigene assay lists only c.2088+1G>A, not c.2088+5G>C, and the method or material behind the statement for this variant is not given. 36211342 counts this among previously reported variants (its reference 32) and reports no new assay for it.

quotes.quote: Additionally, the severity differed between patient 3 (c.2088 + 5G>C) and patient 49 (c.2099 + 1G>A), despite both exhibiting exon 8 skipping (p.H636fsX).

Determination of the patients’ genotypes and TNFAIP3 variants revealed several previously reported variants (32) and as well as two variants (p.Lys329Asn*1 and p.Gly583*) newly confirmed to be pathogenic using a NF-κB reporter gene activity assay (see the method of NF-κB reporter gene activity assay an Figure S2 in the electronic supplemental material).

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Intronic change at +5 of a splice donor; protein not predictable from the cDNA alone (batch: p.?). Both papers state p.His636Glufs*55 / p.His636GlufsX55 (exon 8 skipping). Both papers attribute the disease to heterozygous loss-of-function variants.

quotes.quote: A20 haploinsufficiency (HA20) is a systemic autoinflammatory disease caused by a heterozygous loss-of-function mutation in the TNF-α-induced protein 3 (TNFAIP3).
A20 haploinsufficiency (HA20) is a hereditary autoinflammatory disease caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variants in the TNFAIP3 gene (1).
All 54 patients analyzed had heterozygous variants in TNFAIP3, comprising a total of 35 distinct pathogenic variants.

concerns: Same person: HA20-ID0219 (36211342 #9) and HA20-ID0730 (40574834 P3) are probably one individual (male; sJIA then psoriatic arthritis; same variant; P3's IFN score cites 36211342). Onset differs slightly (1 y vs 10 mo). Count once.

Protein differs from the batch prediction: the papers state p.His636Glufs*55 (exon 8 skipping); the batch gives p.? (protein_check: differs). The source of the exon-skipping evidence for this +5 variant is not stated in these papers.
Carrier missing from the batch: the mother of P3 (10.06% somatic mosaicism, asymptomatic) has no row.

Possible other genetic factor: 31384100 (in this batch) mentions a previously reported HA20 patient with very early-onset psoriatic arthritis, spondylitis and aortic insufficiency who also carried HLA-B27, but does not name the variant, so it is not linked here.
notes_for_panel: One boy reported twice, with an asymptomatic mosaic mother. The exon 8 skipping statement for this variant is asserted in 40574834 without the method shown; the minigene assay in that paper covered c.2088+1G>A only.
